column1: # FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE: Square Enix, Unreal Engine 5.6.1 (SDK MW+EpicGames+UnrealEngine-5_6_1 in main; the desktop renderer, SF_GLSL_SWITCH shaders), SDK 20.5.17, NVN, CRIWARE sound;
# update 1.0.1 (v65536). Everything is in one IoStore container beside one pak; the shader libraries are IoStore chunks (uepak.py).
# Started from the NSP script's provisional profile (dm/games/profile_guess.py) and brought up on the Mac (docs/agents)

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie, which main imports from; the sdk is STEINS;GATE RE:BOOT's build)
# 60 fps (30 on the Switch): the engine's Switch device profile sets rhi.syncinterval=2 (BaseSwitchDeviceProfiles.ini), so the game asks for present interval 2, and the game sets no t.MaxFPS.
# The host writes rhi.SyncInterval 1 into its console variable (hle_fpslock.c), whenever the game sets it back (at level loads), so the game asks for present interval 1 itself. Unreal steps
# the game by the time that really passed: DM_NVN_REGLUM traces of the same keys from the same save at 30 and 60 fps (59.8 fps, frame time p99 18 ms on the Mac) match from the load
# through a 3 s walk (thumbnail difference ≤ 0.006). DM_FPS_TARGET=30 (Documents/env.txt on the iPhone) keeps the game's 30 and saves power
# Unreal Engine 5.6.1: nninitStartup (main+0x13370) reserves one 62 GB region for the engine, and its FMallocBinned3
# (38 GB of address space) is constructed in place in the bss; the constructor call is cut and the host runs Unreal's heap on a malloc zone (dm/tools/ue_malloc.py, hle_uemalloc.c layout UE5_6),
# and the SDK's node area is cut to 62 MB. The engine hands the region out with a page allocator of its own (main+0x13ef0): a bump pointer, and freed blocks kept in free lists by size
# class, so its address use only grows, and past the region's end OnOutOfMemory (main+0x13c74) aborts. Probed at main+0x13fcc from the save in the first field, through the first battle:
# a 1 GB block at boot (a static constructor), the high-water mark at +1.50 GB 15 s in, +1.77 GB at 56 s, +2.02 GB at 166 s; a 2 GB region (DRAGON QUEST VII Reimagined's) aborted in that
# battle. This SDK build aligns regions of 2 MB and more to 2 MB only (VammManager::AllocateAddressRegion, sdk+0x145e00), so the region starts right after the node area, and

# the rewriter's engine-wide gate on the store of its size (dm/tools/ue_region.py; hle_svc.c) gives it what the alias region has room for in Engage's 5 GB block (256 MB in front + 4.375 GB alias region
# + 256 MB stack region + 128 MB heap region): 4.06 GB (until 2026-10-31 -SwitchVirtualAddressSpaceSize=4064 in game_args). On the Mac in the field and the first battle, with 4064 MB:
# about 1 GB of the alias region mapped, an Unreal heap of 1 GB, 2.2-2.4 GB resident and 1.2-1.5 GB of Metal allocations
# the NPDM declares 20 MB of system resource
# A 3D field whose camera the right stick tilts and turns: the 3D pad layout. It plays docked (1920x1080)
# 2,077 vertex shaders (Unreal's particle vertex factories) pick one of several c2 table slots at run time: texture table words 0x168-0x1c0 and sampler table words 0x568-0x590, and no other
# word of c2. The translator cannot trace them to one slot: slot indices in c2, the bound slots in its arrays (without the key the first one aborted the host in a double free, now fixed)
# The two shader libraries of the IoStore container FFRS-Switch.utoc / .ucas (no shader code archive in the pak): the engine's global shaders and the game's material shaders. Their tables and
# shader groups are Oodle-compressed, which the game's own decoder undoes in the Mac host's tool mode (uepak.py Toc / io_archive / OodleHost, no boot). Unreal combines vertex and pixel
# shaders per draw from its pipeline state, so every vertex shader is made to link with any pixel shader (shader_split.py separable_pairs)
